title: Your first minutes in One Mission

chapters.title: Start on The Floor
chapters.narration: Welcome to One Mission. The Floor brings your account, gold context, and AI tools together.
chapters.heading: Welcome to One Mission
chapters.subtitle: Your account and AI tools, together.

chapters.title: Meet Atlas
chapters.narration: Tap Talk to Atlas to speak, or Type a question. Ask, “What’s happening with gold?” Your conversation and generated signals stay right here in the app.
chapters.heading: Meet Atlas
chapters.subtitle: Speak or type. Keep the conversation here.

chapters.title: Choose your AI tool
chapters.narration: OM AI Plays looks for setups in your chosen market. GENX focuses on gold. Pulse scans markets. Gold Command Center is Atlas’s dedicated gold workspace; the Atlas tab opens your in-app assistant.
chapters.heading: Your tools work together
chapters.subtitle: Choose a market, focus on gold, or scan for ideas.

chapters.title: Generate a read
chapters.narration: Choose a market and style, check the displayed cost, and tap Generate play. For GENX, pick Quick, Intraday, or Swing, then Analyze gold.
chapters.heading: Ask for a fresh read
chapters.subtitle: Check the cost shown before you generate.

chapters.title: Understand the setup
chapters.narration: Review the entry, stop, targets, and timeframe breakdown. Tap Explain this signal for help. Read any waiting or unconfirmed label before deciding what to do.
chapters.heading: Understand the setup
chapters.subtitle: Review the levels, reasoning, and current status.

chapters.title: Connect with FLOW
chapters.narration: In FLOW, tap Connect account. Choose Demo or Live, then enter your broker’s Server and TradeLocker email and password. New accounts start with Trading on. Open Manage accounts to check Trading, Follow every GENX signal, risk, and Auto-run FLOW. Enabled automation can place trades without another prompt.
chapters.heading: Connect your broker in FLOW
chapters.subtitle: Review the account’s trading and risk settings.
callouts: New accounts start with Trading on

chapters.title: Review a manual trade
chapters.narration: For a manual trade, open Execute BUY or SELL on the signal. Review the receiving accounts, risk, and size. These tickets place at the current price. Tap Execute, then the final confirmation only when you’re ready.
chapters.heading: Review before you confirm
chapters.subtitle: A manual ticket has its own account and order review.
callouts: Manual tickets place at the current price

chapters.title: Manage trades and view streaks
chapters.narration: Back on The Floor, Active trades shows running pips. Take partial, Breakeven, and Close trade each open a review. Winning streaks separate FLOW on your selected account from GENX community calls.
chapters.heading: Keep track from The Floor
chapters.subtitle: Review each trade change and wait for broker confirmation.

chapters.title: Ask your first question
chapters.narration: AI helps you understand setups. Results aren’t guaranteed. Start by asking Atlas.
chapters.heading: Start with a question
chapters.subtitle: What would you like to understand first?

productionNotes: Chapters and captions follow the narration's model-derived phoneme timings. The final frame holds after the voice finishes.
Use illustrative demo data and masked credentials. The tutorial itself does not connect an account, generate a paid signal, or submit an order.
Keep Trading, Follow every GENX signal, and Auto-run FLOW distinct. New accounts start with Trading on; a never-set Auto-run state is different from explicitly Off.
The five-timeframe breakdown belongs to OM AI Plays. GENX has its own gold read, trigger, and invalidation.
Show the confirmed BUY example with Yes, place buy. Unconfirmed ideas use manual override wording.
Manual tickets place at the current price with a price limit; they do not wait at the play’s displayed limit-entry level or enable automation.
Display FLOW selected-account streaks separately from GENX community callouts, without invented performance counts.
Queue the welcome player and the existing first-visit risk disclosure so only one dialog owns focus at a time.
